hints: Represent one bits by 1 and zero bits by 0.
For distance d, sum s[i]*s[i+d] over valid i.
This correlation becomes a convolution after reversing one copy of the string.
analogy: Slide a reversed copy against the original; each overlap of two ones contributes a match.
example: In 1011, distance 1 has one pair, distance 2 has one, and distance 3 has one.
algorithm: Make an array A of the bits and B as A reversed. Convolve A and B using FFT with careful rounding or an exact NTT. For each distance d from 1 to n-1, output coefficient n-1+d.
correctness: The coefficient at n-1+d sums A[i+d]*A[i] over all valid i, so it counts exactly pairs of one bits separated by d.
complexity: For length n, O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
